'''('''CARP''') ({{IPA|es|ˈkluβ aˈtletiko ˈriβer ˈpleit}}) is an Argentine professional [[sports club]] based in the [[Belgrano, Buenos Aires|Belgrano]] neighborhood of [[Buenos Aires]]. Founded in 1901,{{refn|group=note1|name=foundation}} the club is named after the English-language name for the city's [[estuary]], [[Río de la Plata]]. River's home stadium, the [[Estadio Monumental (Buenos Aires)|Monumental]], is the largest in South America. River had the highest average home attendance of any association football club in the world in 2023 with 84,567. With more than 350,000 members at the end of 2023, River is one of the [[List of sports clubs by membership|largest sports clubs by membership]]. It repeated this achievement in 2024 and 2025. With 72 official titles to date[https://www.ole.com.ar/futbol-primera/campeones-tabla-titulos-locales-futbol-argentino_0_W26EJ4mLPo.html Con Belgrano campeón, ¿cómo quedó la tabla de títulos?] on ole.com.ar[https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2026/05/24/con-la-historica-consagracion-de-belgrano-ante-river-asi-quedo-la-tabla-de-titulos-del-futbol-argentino/ Con la histórica consagración de Belgrano ante River, así quedó la tabla de títulos] on infobae.com. 24 May 2026, River Plate is one of most successful clubs among Argentina’s traditional ''[[Big Five (Argentine football)|Big Five]]'' of [[Football in Argentina|Argentine football]].[https://www.ambito.com/deportes/como-nacieron-los-cinco-grandes-del-futbol-argentino-la-regla-afa-que-se-consolido-la-historia-n6174432 Cómo nacieron los cinco grandes del fútbol argentino] on ambito.com, 5 Aug 2025 Although a [[Multi-sports club|multi-sport club]], River Plate is best known for its professional [[association football]] department, which has won Argentina's [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]] championship [[List of Argentine Primera División champions|a record 38 times]], most recently in [[2023 Argentine Primera División|2023]]. River Plate have also won 16 [[List of Argentine football national cups|national cups]], making River Argentina's most successful team in domestic competitions with 54 titles in total.{{Cite web |last1=Gorgazzi |first1=Osvaldo José |last2=Villa Martínez |first2=Héctor |date=31 October 2023 |title=Argentina – List of Champions and Runners-Up |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/argchamp.html |access-date=2 January 2024 |publisher=RSSSF}}{{Cite web |last1=Gorgazzi |first1=Osvaldo José |date=5 March 2023 |title=Argentina – Domestic Cup History |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/argcuphist.html |access-date=2 January 2024 |publisher=RSSSF}} At international level, River have won 18 titles, including four [[Copa Libertadores]], one [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]], one [[Supercopa Sudamericana]], one [[Copa Sudamericana]], three [[Recopa Sudamericana|Recopa Sudamericanas]], one [[Copa Interamericana]], one [[Suruga Bank Championship]], a record five [[Copa Aldao|Copa Aldaos]], and one [[Tie Cup]].{{Cite web |title=Títles |url=http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/campeonatos-international-62 |access-date=2 January 2024 |publisher=CA River Plate}} In addition, River Plate's [[reserve team]] won the [[U-20 Copa Libertadores]] in [[2012 U-20 Copa Libertadores|2012]]. After winning the [[2014 Copa Sudamericana]], [[2015 Recopa Sudamericana]] and the [[2015 Copa Libertadores]], River Plate became the first team to simultaneously hold [[CONMEBOL]]'s three current major international competitions.{{cite web|url=http://tgpost.com.ar/los-titulos-internacionales-logrados-por-gallardo-como-tecnico-de-river/|title=Los títulos internacionales logrados por Gallardo como técnico de River|last=Rocca|first=Santiago|date=12 August 2015|publisher=TG News|language=es|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151118072305/http://tgpost.com.ar/los-titulos-internacionales-logrados-por-gallardo-como-tecnico-de-river/|archive-date=18 November 2015|access-date=13 August 2015}}{{cite web|date=12 August 2015|title=El fenómeno River|url=http://www.clarin.com/deportes/futbol/river-plate/River-Suruga_Bank-Marcelo_Gallardo-Copa_Libertadores-Mundial_de_Clubes_0_1411059047.html|url-status=live|access-date=2015-08-13|website=Clarin.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150813155557/http://www.clarin.com:80/deportes/futbol/river-plate/River-Suruga_Bank-Marcelo_Gallardo-Copa_Libertadores-Mundial_de_Clubes_0_1411059047.html |archive-date=13 August 2015 }} River Plate are ranked first in the [[all-time Argentine Primera División table]], having gained the most points, having played the most matches, and having the highest win percentage. River are also ranked first in the [[historical table of the Copa Libertadores]], being the South American team with most games won and the most points gained.{{cite web |last=Aldo Colombo and Ricardo Pontes |date=29 February 2012 |title=Copa Libertadores – All-Time Table (1960–2011) |url=https://www.rsssf.org/sacups/copalibpts.html |access-date=9 December 2018 |website=[[RSSSF]]}} The club were placed ninth in the [[FIFA Club of the Century]] poll in 2000.{{cite web |title=FIFA Club of the Century |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/fifa-awards.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112042845/http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/fifa-awards.html |archive-date=12 January 2016 |access-date=23 March 2015 |website=[[RSSSF]]}} In a survey published by the [[Argentine Football Association]] in 2016, 6 out of 11 players of the all-time greatest Argentina national team had played for River Plate.{{cite web|title = La Selección de todos los tiempos|url = https://www.afa.com.ar/es/posts/la-seleccion-de-todos-los-tiempos|website = www.afa.org.ar|access-date = 2016-02-07}} River have a fierce rivalry with [[Boca Juniors]]. Matches between them are known as the [[Superclásico]], and the rivalry is among the most heated in the sport, due to the fixture's global popularity and both clubs having the most fans in Argentina. Notable players who have played for River include [[José Manuel Moreno]], [[Ángel Labruna]], [[Adolfo Pedernera]], [[Amadeo Carrizo]], [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], [[Omar Sívori]], [[Norberto Alonso]], [[Daniel Passarella]], [[Enzo Francescoli]], [[Roberto Ayala]], [[Ariel Ortega]], [[Marcelo Salas]], [[Hernán Crespo]], [[Marcelo Gallardo]], [[Pablo Aimar]], [[Javier Saviola]], [[Javier Mascherano]], [[Radamel Falcao]], [[Gonzalo Higuaín]] and [[Enzo Fernández]]. ==History== {{main|History of Club Atlético River Plate}} [[File:River_ascenso_1908.jpg|left|thumb|The team that achieved the promotion to first division in 1908.]] According with the club's official history, River Plate was founded on 25 May 1901,{{refn|group=note1|name=foundation}} close to the [[La Boca]] neighborhood (later the home of fierce rivals [[Boca Juniors]]). They were formed from the merger of two clubs, "Santa Rosa" and "La Rosales", with Leopoldo Bard elected as the first president. The name River Plate was chosen because of an incident during the construction of Buenos Aires Port: one of the members had seen how the workers of Dique nº 3 left their duties for a while to play a football match. The boxes they were working with just said "The River Plate" (the name the English gave to the [[Río de la Plata]]) and that inscription was taken to name the new club. River Plate affiliated to the [[Argentine Football Association]] in 1905, debuting in the third division against Facultad de Medicina. On 13 December 1908, the team was promoted to first division after beating [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]] 2–1. However, the match was declared null due to River supporters jumping onto the field to celebrate with the players, so a new match had to be played. River again won, this time 7–0, to achieve promotion. In 1914 River won its first domestic championship, the [[Copa de Competencia Jockey Club]]{{Cite web |title=Argentina - Copa de Competencia "Jockey Club" - 1914 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/arg-joc14.html |access-date=2024-09-05 |website=www.rsssf.org}} and its first international title, the [[Tie Cup|Copa de Competencia Chevallier Boutell]]. The nickname ''Los Millonarios'' came after the acquisition of winger [[Carlos Peucelle]] in 1931 for $10,000 and [[Bernabé Ferreyra]] for $35,000 (a large sum of money for the period) in [[1932 Argentine Primera División|1932]]. In the following years, River Plate consolidated its place as one of the most popular teams of Argentina, and the 20th century brought much success. The club's record of 28 official tournaments saw them dubbed ''El Campeón del Siglo'' (The Champions of the Century).{{cite web| url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/166487-el-campeon-del-siglo| title=El 2026|website=[[Infobae]]|language=es-AR}}]] As in many football shirts and sports in general, the team's jersey has a badge on its front, as a symbol of the institution. When the River Plate jersey was created it did not have a badge, and its presence varied throughout the history, according to the designs of each era.[https://www.primeroriver.com/secciones/escudo "Escudo de River Plate"] on ''Primeroriver.com'', 26 December 2016 Currently it is embroidered on the jersey, with three colors (red, white and black). Its format resembles that of the jersey, as it has a red stripe that crosses it, along with the acronym of the club (CARP) in black, and the background is white, in a stylized design. When Hugo Santilli became chairman in 1984, he soon called to a competition where a new emblem would be chosen. The main objective of this new image was to eradicate the nickname ''Gallinas (Hens)'' that River's rivals (Boca Juniors fans mainly) used to mock them. Artists from Argentina took part in that competition. The club finally chose a logo designed by Claudio Loiseau (brother of cartoonist [[Carlos Loiseau|Caloi]]).[https://noticiasargentinas.com/deportes/la-verdadera-historia-del-leon-de-river-y-el-fallido-intento-de-boca-por-copiarlo La verdadera historia del león de River y el fallido intento de Boca por copiarlo] by Pablo Tallón on Noticias Argentinas, 8 Mar 2021 This emblem showed the figure of a lion (wearing a River jersey) rising from the Monumental stadium. {{cquote|We had to get into (lion figures) to avoid replicating symbols such as [[Plaza Hotel Buenos Aires|Plaza Hotel]]'s or [[Peugeot]]'s. Carlos (Loiseau) contacted designer [[Ronald Shakespear]], who got us a bunch of lion designs... Carlos brought out ideas but he was not a designer but a cartoonist. Once he finished with that, I made the final drawing"|author= Claudio Loiseau, designer of the lion emblem.}} Once it was approved, the lion logo was added to the uniforms, debuting in 1985. With that emblem on their chests, River Plate won the [[Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores de América]] and [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|European/South American Cup]].[https://www.tycsports.com/river-plate/a-40-anos-del-debut-de-un-leon-en-la-camiseta-de-river-el-isotipo-campeon-que-desperto-la-reaccion-de-boca-id634923.html A 40 años del debut de un león en la camiseta de River, el isotipo campeón que despertó la reacción de Boca] by Andrés Burgo, 13 Feb 2025 In 1989, when Santilli left the club so the lion went with him and has not been reestablished since.[https://www.goal.com/es/noticias/escudo-de-river-historia-y-diseno/7hntvugdvvma1wwjlszyoufet Escudo de River Plate: historia y diseño] by Carlos Martínez on Goal.com {{in lang|es}} In February 2022, River Plate launched its new corporate image, which included an update to the logo and a typography designed exclusively for the club. The corporate image was created and developed by "Grupo Berro", a [[brand]]ing and design studio that had been working on the corporate image for over two years.[https://www.minutouno.com/deportes/river/la-historia-detras-del-nuevo-escudo-n5378262 La historia detrás del nuevo escudo de River] on Minuto Uno, 22 Feb 2022[https://www.tycsports.com/river-plate/nuevo-escudo-river-como-se-creo-id414376.html Los detalles de cómo se creó el nuevo escudo de River] on TyC Sports, 23 Feb 2022[https://grupoberro.com/es/trabajos/club-atletico-river-plate-2021 Club Atlético River Plate - Branding & Identidad. Estrategia de comunicación] on Grupo Berro ==Rivalry== {{main|Superclásico}} River Plate and [[Boca Juniors]] are the two largest football clubs in Argentina, with more than half the country's football fans supporting the clubs. Due to the rivalry between them, the Boca Juniors vs River Plate ''[[Major football rivalries#Boca Juniors vs River Plate|Superclásico]]'' [[local derby]] match was listed by the [[BBC]] as one of the most famous derbies in the world.{{Cite news |date=2002-10-05 |title=Boca Juniors v River Plate |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sportacademy/hi/sa/football/features/newsid_2297000/2297495.stm |access-date=2024-09-05 |language=en-GB}} Attending the match was also acclaimed in 2004 as the number one of the ''Fifty sporting things you must do before you die'' by ''[[The Observer]]''.{{Cite web |title=50 sporting things you must do before you die {{!}} Sport {{!}} The Observer |url=https://www.theguardian.com/observer/osm/story/0,6903,1182710,00.html |access-date=2024-09-05 |website=www.theguardian.com}} ==Club nicknames== [[File:La Maquina.jpg|thumb|left|''[[La Máquina]]'' in 1941. Fltr: [[Juan Carlos Muñoz (footballer, born 1919)|Muñoz]], [[José Manuel Moreno|Moreno]], [[Adolfo Pedernera|Pedernera]], [[Ángel Labruna|Labruna]], [[Félix Loustau|Loustau]]]] The "River Plate" name was chosen in 1901, when the team was still located at the [[La Boca]] neighbourhood, next to the [[Río de la Plata]] ("River Plate" in some English sources). Proposed names as "Club Atlético Forward", "Juventud Boquense" or "La Rosales" had been rejected. Pedro Martínez saw the name "The River Plate" written at ship containers, and proposed it as a name, which was finally accepted as the official name.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cariverplate.com.ar/el-club/historia|title=River Plate - Sitio Oficial|first=Club Atletico River|last=Plate|website=caRiverPlate.com.ar}} River fans and the media commonly use the nickname ''Los Millonarios'' (The Millionaires) for the club. The name originated from the 1930s following some expensive player transfers from other clubs, including [[Carlos Peucelle]] from [[Club Sportivo Buenos Aires|Sportivo Buenos Aires]] in 1931 and [[Bernabé Ferreyra]] from [[Club Atlético Tigre|Tigre]] in 1932.[https://www.goal.com/es-ar/noticias/por-que-a-river-plate-le-dicen-millonarios/1dc525qhwdrh71ii1khx6rfpa7 ¿Por qué a River Plate le dicen Millonarios?], Goal.com, 9 December 2018 Due to the red band in their shirt, it is also common to refer to River as ''El Equipo de la Banda'' (the team with the band) or simply ''La Banda'' (which means "the stripe", but can also mean "the band" -both as in "gang" and "musical group"). River Plate's [[Forward (association football)|forwards]] between 1941 and 1946 were given the nickname ''[[La Máquina]]'' (The Machine), due to their synchronization and movements on the field.[https://www.elgrafico.com.ar/articulo/1088/5076/la-maquina-de-riverv La Máquina de River] by Matías Rodríguez, ''El Gráfico'', 28 February 2014 There was also a River Plate team that was known as ''La Maquinita'' (The Little Machine, as tribute to its predecessor) in the 1950s. Managed by [[José María Minella]], the team earned the nickname after winning five championships in six years (1952–57).[https://www.clarin.com/deportes/hazana-inolvidable_0_BJxgRiNxRKe.html Una hazaña inolvidable], ''Clarín'', 22 June 2002 Some notable players were [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], [[Santiago Vernazza]], [[Walter Gómez]], [[Enrique Omar Sívori]], among others. Some members of the original ''Máquina'' of the 1940s such as Labruna and Loustau, were also part of the team.[https://www.lanacion.com.ar/2081676-murio-santiago-vernazza-ex-integrante-de-la-maquinita-de-river Murió Santiago Vernazza, ex integrante de "La Maquinita" de River], ''La Nación'', 12 November 2017 ==Stadiums== [[File:Canchariver1920.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The stadium built by River Plate in [[La Boca]]. The club played its home games there from 1915 to 1923.]] The [[Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti|Estadio Antonio Liberti]] (nicknamed ''El Monumental'') located in the [[Belgrano, Buenos Aires|Belgrano]] [[barrios of Buenos Aires|neighborhood]] of [[Buenos Aires]] is River Plate's stadium. It was inaugurated on 25 May 1938, and its current capacity is 85,018 spectators, following renovations completed in 2025. thirteen titles. Gallardo (appointed in 2014) was the club's manager until November 2022 and under his direction, River Plate won most of its international championships. Domestic titles won include three [[Copa Argentina]] ([[2015–16 Copa Argentina|2015–16]], [[2016–17 Copa Argentina|2016–17]] and [[2018–19 Copa Argentina|2018–19]]) and two [[Supercopa Argentina]] ([[2017 Supercopa Argentina|2017]], [[2019 Supercopa Argentina|2019]]). He has been specially successful in the international scene, having won two [[Copa Libertadores]] ([[Copa Libertadores de América|2015]], [[Copa Libertadores de América|2018]]), one [[Copa Sudamericana]] ([[2014 Copa Sudamericana|2014]]), three [[Recopa Sudamericana]] ([[2015 Recopa Sudamericana|2015]], [[2016 Recopa Sudamericana|2016]], [[2019 Recopa Sudamericana|2019]]), and one [[Suruga Bank Championship]] ([[2015 Suruga Bank Championship|2015]]). Several of these championship wins included memorable victories against archrivals [[Boca Juniors]]. [[Ramón Díaz]] had three tenures on River Plate (1995–2000, 2001–02, and 2012–14), being the club's most successful manager in the domestic scene, having achieved six [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]] titles ([[1996–97 Argentine Primera División#Torneo Apertura|1996–97 Torneo Apertura]], [[1996–97 Argentine Primera División#Torneo Clausura|1996–97 Torneo Clausura]], [[1997–98 Argentine Primera División#Torneo Apertura|1997–98 Torneo Apertura]], [[1999–2000 Argentine Primera División#Torneo Apertura|1999–2000 Torneo Apertura]], [[2001–02 Argentine Primera División#Torneo Clausura ("Closing" Tournament)|2001–02 Torneo Clausura]], [[2013–14 Argentine Primera División season#Torneo Final|2013–14 Torneo Final]]) and one Copa Campeonato ([[2013–14 Argentine Primera División season#Superfinal|2014]]){{refn|The "Superfinal" is considered as a national cup by the [[Argentine Football Association]].[http://canchallena.lanacion.com.ar/1695307-la-afa-homologo-la-superfinal-de-river-como-una-copa-nacional "La AFA homologó la Superfinal de River como una Copa Nacional", Cancha Llena.com] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304003108/http://canchallena.lanacion.com.ar/1695307-la-afa-homologo-la-superfinal-de-river-como-una-copa-nacional |date=4 March 2016 }}, 28 May 2014}}; internationally, he won the [[Copa Libertadores]] ([[1996 Copa Libertadores|1996]]) and one [[Supercopa Libertadores]] ([[1997 Supercopa Libertadores|1997]]). [[José María Minella]] was another notable manager with eight titles won with River Plate, seven Primera División championships ([[1945 Argentine Primera División|1945]], [[1947 Argentine Primera División|1947]], [[1952 Argentine Primera División|1952]], [[1953 Argentine Primera División|1953]], [[1955 Argentine Primera División|1955]], [[1956 Argentine Primera División|1956]], [[1957 Argentine Primera División|1957]]) and one [[Copa Aldao|Copa Dr. Ricardo Aldao]] (1947). won the [[1950 FIBA World Championship|1950 World Cup]] with [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]]]] The [[basketball]] team currently plays in the Torneo Federal de Básquetbol. In 1950, the [[1950 FIBA World Championship|first FIBA World Championship]] was played in Buenos Aires and [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]] claimed the gold medal with 3 River Plate players: [[Alberto López (basketball)|Alberto López]], [[Leopoldo Contarbio]] and Vito Liva. The club won a [[Campeonato Argentino de Clubes|Campeonato Argentino]] title in 1983, and finished in the 2nd place in the [[Campeonato Sudamericano de Clubes Campeones de Básquetbol]] in 1984. The last edition of the Campeonato Argentino was held in that year, and River Plate was defeated in the finals, then playing at its successor competition, [[Liga Nacional de Básquetbol]], between 1985–93 and 2004–06. The team reached the finals in 1988, and for the 1989 and 1990 seasons, [[Héctor Campana]] became the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet Statistical Leaders|top scorer of the LNB]], playing for River Plate. The team also achieved 2nd place in 2004 and 2005 editions of Copa Argentina. Since 2014, after eight years of absence in professional basketball, River Plate returned to national tournaments playing the [[Argentine Basketball Federation|CABB]] Federal Basketball Tournament.{{cite web |title=Básquet |url=http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/basquet |website=cariverplate.com.ar |access-date=14 February 2019}} ===Field hockey=== [[File:River Plate Ciudad hockey P1520799 resize (5564230061).jpg|thumb|left|180px|River Plate field hockey team playing [[Club Ciudad de Buenos Aires|Club Ciudad]] in 2011]] The women's [[field hockey]] team is affiliated to the [[Buenos Aires Hockey Association]] (AHBA)[http://www.guiadeclubesahba.com.ar/ Guia de Clubes at AHBA website], 11 October 2014 and currently playing in [[Metropolitano de Hockey (Women)|Torneo Metropolitano A]], the top division of regional hockey in Argentina. In 2016, the squad (nicknamed ''Las Vikingas'') won its first [[Metropolitano de Hockey (Women)|Metropolitano]] championship after beating [[Club Ciudad de Buenos Aires|Ciudad de Buenos Aires]] by 3–2 at the final.[http://www.clarin.com/deportes/hockey/River-Ciudad-Metropolitano-femenino-historia_0_1702029886.html River dio vuelta la final ante Ciudad y salió campeón del Metropolitano femenino por primera vez en su historia], ''Clarín'', 9 December 2016 In 2017, ''Las Vikingas'' won their third consecutive Hockey National League after defeating [[Club Italiano]] by 2–0 at the final, thus becoming one of the two clubs with most titles at the national tournament.{{cite web |title=River Three-Times National Champion |url=http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/river-three-times-national-champion |website=cariverplate.com.ar |access-date=14 February 2019}} Two players from River Plate, [[Lucina von der Heyde]] and [[Bianca Donati]], who were [[2016 Women's Hockey Junior World Cup|Junior World Champions in Chile 2016]], made their debut in a world cup in [[2018 Women's Hockey World Cup|London 2018]]. Von der Heyde was named the [[FIH Player of the Year Awards|FIH Rising Star of the Year]].{{cite web |title=De Goede & Van Doren named Players of the Year in 2018 FIH Hockey Stars Awards |url=http://fih.ch/events/hockey-stars-awards/hockey-stars-2018/news/de-goede-van-doren-named-players-of-the-year-in-2018-fih-hockey-stars-awards/ |website=fih.ch |access-date=14 February 2019}} {{-}} ===Futsal=== The [[futsal]] team plays in the [[Argentine División de Honor de Futsal|Argentine División de Honor]]. The team won three championships in 1991, 2002 and 2003, and two Copa Argentina de Futsal in 2016 and 2017.{{cite news |title=River se consagró bicampeón de la Copa Argentina de futsal |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/2080823-river-se-consagro-bicampeon-de-la-copa-argentina-de-futsal |newspaper=La Nación |date=10 November 2017 |access-date=14 February 2019}} The team also achieved a third place in the [[Copa Libertadores de Futsal]] in 2013.{{cite web |title=Podio histórico |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/-/podio-historico_0_HJabyeFkj2l.html |website=ole.com.ar |date=13 December 2013 |access-date=14 February 2019}} ===Handball=== River is one of the founding clubs of the Federación Metropolitana de Balonmano (Fe.Me.Bal.) and it is also the institution that won more championships in local history.{{cite web |title=Handball |url=http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/handball |website=cariverplate.com.ar |access-date=14 February 2019}} All these titles have been obtained in the metropolitan and national levels, either in Metropolitan, Aperturas, Clausuras, Super 4 or Nacionales Tournaments, or the Federal League. The men's team won 32 domestic titles and the gold medal in the [[South American Men's Club Handball Championship]] in 1984.{{cite web |title=Men's Clubs Senior Panamerican Competitions |url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?url=http://panamhandball.org/pathf/documentos/PATHF-hist-club-m.pdf&chrome=true |website=panamhandball.org |access-date=14 February 2019}} The team also achieved 2 Bronze medals in the same competition and 4 Bronze medals in the [[Pan American Men's Club Handball Championship]]. The women's team won 9 national titles, and the silver medal in the [[South American Women's Club Handball Championship]] in 1984 and the bronze medal in 1987.{{cite web |title=Women's Clubs Senior Pan American Competitions |url=http://panamhandball.org/pathf/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Competiciones-Panam-y-Regionales-Clubes-Adulto-Fem-2017.pdf |website=panamhandball.org |access-date=14 February 2019}} The more prominent players in the club's history are Guillermo Till, Claudio Straffe, Freddy Ambrosini, Gabriel Canzoniero and Juan Ojea. ===Swimming=== [[File:Meolans BA Deporte.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[José Meolans]] competed for River Plate and represented Argentina in four [[Summer Olympics|Olympic Games]]]] The current swimming team has its origins in 2003, after many years in which the Club Atlético River Plate had no representatives in the national championships of this discipline. The draft to form the best team in the country was led by Professor Rodolfo Sacco and had the best results that had never been achieved in the institution. The team began to form from a contractual relationship with the swimmer [[José Meolans]],[https://www.lanacion.com.ar/664772-river-meolans-y-un-trabajo-en-equipo River, Meolans y un trabajo en equipo] on ''La Nación'', 20 December 2004 one of the Argentine swimmers with most titles won.[https://www.lavoz.com.ar/numero-cero/retrato-de-jose-meolans-hombre-al-agua Retrato de José Meolans], ''La Voz'', 16 November 2016 Many high-level swimmers, trained in other institutions began to approach to be part of what would be the best team in the country for the coming years.{{cite web |title=Natación |url=http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/natacion |website=cariverplate.com.ar |access-date=14 February 2019}} Other swimmers from River Plate who represented Argentina in the Olympics include Meolans himself, [[Georgina Bardach]], [[Eduardo Germán Otero]], [[Walter Arciprete]], [[Agustín Fiorilli]], [[María del Pilar Pereyra]], [[Juan Pereyra]], [[Damián Blaum]], [[Javiera Salcedo]], [[Pablo Martín Abal]], [[Cecilia Biagioli]]. ===Tennis=== Tennis has been played at River Plate since 1923.[http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/tenis Tenis] on River Plate website The facilities at River include ten clay courts and one hard court. The club fields many teams in official tournaments organized by the Asociación Argentina de Tenis (AAT), and hosts competitions and programs aimed at developing tennis in Argentina.{{cite web |title=Tenis |url=http://www.cariverplate.com.ar/tenis |website=cariverplate.com.ar |access-date=14 February 2019}} [[Gabriela Sabatini]], who is considered the best Argentine women's tennis player in history and an icon in national women's sport, began practicing at River at age 6, under the direction of Professor Daniel Fidalgo, with whom she trained for seven years.
